governing_rule: A foreclosure timeline is a chain of different legal events, not one deadline. Verification and applicability are separate questions.

supports: Covered pre-NOD borrower-contact and due-diligence requirements; applicability is limited by the statute.

For mortgages/deeds of trust described in §2924.15 and subject to the statutory entity exception, a complete first-lien loan-modification application submitted at least five business days before sale can restrict NOD, notice-of-sale, and trustee-sale activity while pending; denial/appeal and resumption rules are separately stated.
Core nonjudicial foreclosure sequence beginning with recording the NOD and the statutory waiting period before the sale-notice stage.
Statutory reinstatement is distinct from redemption and loan modification and is subject to the statute and loan-specific conditions.

For the ordinary power-of-sale procedure covered by subdivision (b)(1), the notice of sale must be publicly posted at least 20 days before sale and published once a week for three consecutive calendar weeks; additional content, posting, publication, residential-property, mailing, recipient, and exception provisions must not be collapsed into one service rule.

Current trustee-sale postponement mechanics: authorized grounds; public-declaration notice of postponement and new date/time/place in ordinary cases; no other postponement notice ordinarily required by subdivision (d); new §2924f sale notice after postponements totaling more than 365 days; separate seven-day rules after specified court orders/stays and separate bankruptcy treatment.

Restrictions on recording a NOD or notice of sale or conducting a trustee sale while a borrower is complying with specified approved written foreclosure-prevention alternatives, subject to statutory coverage and entity limitations.

HBOR remedies for material violations of listed provisions: pre-sale injunctive relief, post-sale actual economic damages where an uncorrected material violation caused loss, enhanced damages for qualifying intentional/reckless/willful misconduct, correction-before-sale limits, bona-fide-purchaser sale-validity protection, attorney fees, and §2924.18(b) entity exclusion.
Separate small-servicer foreclosure-prevention rules and the entity categories referenced as exceptions from specified HBOR provisions; applies only to mortgages/deeds of trust described in §2924.15.

A writ of possession states that occupants face removal if the property is not vacated within five days from service of the writ copy on the occupant, or for a posted copy, within five days from service on the judgment debtor; remaining personal property follows separate statutory handling.

authorities.citation: Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act, Pub. L. 111-22 § 702, as restored
supports: An immediate successor after covered foreclosure generally takes subject to at least 90 days' notice to vacate for a bona fide tenant and, subject to statutory exceptions, the remaining term of a bona fide lease; bona fide tenancy has statutory conditions.

VA foreclosure-avoidance counseling and current VA-guaranteed-loan assistance, including the 2026 Partial Claim Program, loan-technician assistance, and current retention/exit options; VA guaranty does not mean VA owns or services the loan.

Post-foreclosure unlawful detainer under §1161a(b)(3) requires a sale in accordance with Civil Code §2924 under the deed-of-trust power of sale and title under the sale to have been duly perfected; the statute provides a post-sale possession route distinct from ordinary tenant protections.

authorities.citation: Dr. Leevil, LLC v. Westlake Health Care Center, 6 Cal.5th 474 (2018)
supports: California Supreme Court held that §1161a(b)(3) conditions, including duly perfected title, are prerequisites before serving the notice to quit; title perfection in that context requires recording the trustee’s deed.

default_servicing_problem.label: DEFAULT / SERVICING PROBLEM

clock.display: For loans and entities covered by §2923.5, NOD recording is restricted until 30 days after the required contact or statutory due diligence, subject to the statute's applicability limits.

warnings: Do not infer that a violation automatically voids a foreclosure sale.
California procedure and federal Regulation X are separate layers.

notice_of_default.label: NOTICE OF DEFAULT

clock.display: Civil Code §2924 requires not less than three months to elapse after the NOD is recorded before the ordinary sale-notice stage, subject to the statute's sequencing rules.

warnings: This is not a generic promise of exactly 90 days.
Use the recorded NOD date, not the date the borrower happened to read it.

reinstatement.label: REINSTATEMENT

clock.display: Section 2924c's statutory notice describes reinstatement as normally available until five business days before the scheduled sale, subject to statutory and loan-specific conditions.

warnings: Reinstatement is not redemption.
Reinstatement is not a guaranteed loan modification.

notice_of_trustees_sale.label: NOTICE OF TRUSTEE'S SALE

clock.display: For the ordinary §2924f(b)(1) power-of-sale procedure, the written notice of sale must be publicly posted at least 20 days before the scheduled sale; publication and recipient-specific notice duties are separate requirements.

warnings: Do not describe §2924f as merely '20 days notice.' Mailing, posting, publication, content, recipient classes, and exceptions are separate legal requirements.
NOD timing and trustee-sale notice timing are different legal events.

sale_postponed.label: FORECLOSURE SALE POSTPONED / NEW DATE
warnings: Current §2924g ordinarily uses public declaration at the time and place last appointed for sale, stating the reason and new date, time, and place; subdivision (d) says no other postponement notice ordinarily need be given.
If postponements total more than 365 days from the sale date in the notice of sale, further sale proceedings require a new notice of sale under §2924f.
Court-order, operation-of-law stay, bankruptcy, and force-majeure situations have distinct mechanics; do not reduce them to one generic postponement deadline.
The previously merged 10-business-day/5-business-day clock remains withdrawn and must not be restored.

hbor_coverage.label: HBOR COVERAGE CHECK
warnings: HBOR applicability is not universal. Confirm the mortgage/deed of trust is within §2924.15, whether the servicer/entity falls under the main HBOR provisions or the separate §2924.18 small-servicer regime, application completeness, first-lien status, prior evaluation/material change, and sale timing before presenting a protection as applicable.
California HBOR and federal Regulation X are separate legal authorities.

hbor_complete_application.label: COMPLETE FIRST-LIEN LOAN-MODIFICATION APPLICATION

clock.display: For mortgages/deeds of trust within §2924.15 and subject to statutory exceptions, §2923.6 applies when a complete first-lien loan-modification application is submitted at least five business days before the scheduled sale.

warnings: HBOR applicability is not universal; property, lien, borrower, servicer/entity, application completeness, prior evaluation, and timing can matter.
California HBOR and federal Regulation X are separate protections.

hbor_denial_appeal.label: LOAN-MODIFICATION DENIAL / APPEAL

clock.display: For a denial governed by §2923.6(d), the borrower has at least 30 days from the date of the written denial to appeal and provide evidence that the determination was in error.

warnings: Do not apply this appeal clock without first confirming §2923.6 coverage and the statutory exceptions.
Section 2923.6(e) separately restricts foreclosure activity after denial and during a qualifying appeal; do not collapse that resumption rule into the 30-day appeal clock.

hbor_remedies.label: HBOR REMEDIES — PRE-SALE / POST-SALE
warnings: Before recordation of a trustee's deed, §2924.12 may support injunctive relief for a material violation of the listed HBOR sections; relief depends on statutory coverage and materiality.

After recordation of a trustee's deed, §2924.12 provides actual-economic-damages relief for an uncorrected material violation of listed sections and permits enhanced damages only under the statute's intentional/reckless/willful-misconduct standard.
A violation corrected and remedied before the trustee's deed is recorded does not create liability under §2924.12.
Do not state that any HBOR violation automatically voids a sale; §2924.12 expressly protects sale validity in favor of a bona fide purchaser for value without notice.
Section 2924.12 does not apply to entities described in §2924.18(b).

trustee_sale_completed.label: TRUSTEE SALE ALREADY HAPPENED
warnings: A completed sale is not a promise that title can be reversed.
Sale does not itself equal immediate physical eviction; possession procedure is separate.

post_sale_former_owner.label: POST-SALE — FORMER BORROWER / OWNER OCCUPANT
warnings: For the §1161a(b)(3) post-foreclosure possession route, the purchaser must establish a sale in accordance with Civil Code §2924 and duly perfected title.
Dr. Leevil holds that the statutory conditions, including perfected title and recording of the trustee’s deed, must be satisfied before the notice to quit is served.
Do not automatically apply bona-fide-tenant protections to the former borrower/owner, but do not treat the trustee sale itself as permission for immediate physical lockout.
The exact notice-computation clock remains unpublished until service and generally applicable computation rules are fully reconciled.

post_sale_bona_fide_tenant.label: POST-SALE — BONA FIDE TENANT

clock.display: For a tenancy meeting the federal PTFA definition after a covered foreclosure, the immediate successor generally must provide at least 90 days' notice before the effective date of a notice to vacate; qualifying leases can receive additional protection subject to the statute.

warnings: Do not say all tenants get 90 days. The tenancy must satisfy the federal bona-fide requirements, including the statutory relationship, arm's-length, and rent conditions.
Federal PTFA protection does not replace California court eviction procedure or stronger state/local protections.

post_sale_other_or_unknown_occupant.label: POST-SALE — OTHER TENANT / UNKNOWN OCCUPANT
warnings: Identify occupant status, lease, relationship to the former owner, and purchaser before applying a post-foreclosure notice rule. Unknown status means unknown protection, not no protection.

sheriff_writ_execution.label: WRIT / SHERIFF EXECUTION

clock.display: CCP §715.010(b)(2) states five days from service of a copy of the writ on the occupant, or if the writ copy is posted, five days from service of a copy on the judgment debtor, before the levying officer removes occupants.

warnings: Do not paraphrase this as simply five days after receiving notice.
Personal property remaining after possession is delivered is governed separately; do not imply the sheriff necessarily removes or stores it.

hoa_foreclosure.label: HOA FORECLOSURE
warnings: Do not reuse mortgage-foreclosure deadlines.

tax_foreclosure.label: TAX FORECLOSURE
warnings: Unknown means not verified, not no deadline.

court_foreclosure_paper.label: COURT / JUDICIAL FORECLOSURE PAPER
warnings: Route immediately to legal help until procedure is verified.

va_home_loan_default.label: VA-GUARANTEED HOME LOAN IN DEFAULT
warnings: VA usually guarantees rather than owns or services the loan.
VA assistance does not automatically halt California foreclosure.
The VA Partial Claim Program is open in 2026; servicers have an implementation period, so availability through a particular servicer can depend on implementation and eligibility.

priority_questions: Are you currently in qualifying military service?
Do you have a foreclosure sale date?
Have you submitted a complete loss-mitigation application?
If the sale occurred, are you the former owner, a bona fide tenant, another tenant, or is occupant status unclear?
publication_limits: No unverified deadline renders as actionable legal advice.
Regulation X and SCRA remain federal overlays, not California authority.
VA guaranty is not ownership or servicing.
HOA and tax foreclosure remain separate and null-safe until verified.
HBOR coverage must be established before a protection or remedy is presented as applicable.
A null clock is a safety feature when the applicable computation has not been fully verified.
